title: Node-swap latency budgeting and rolling safe deployments
creator: Maya Liu
description:
Problem: During node replacements, rolling upgrades, and proactive maintenance we observe transient tail-latency spikes and throughput regressions that disproportionately affect small tenants and P50-sensitive routes. Current drain behavior is all-or-nothing and lacks a per-tenant latency budget or staged swap policy. This leads to manual intervention, emergency capacity reservations, and suboptimal cost profiles for Dedicated customers.

Goal: Implement a deterministic node-swap/playbook that guarantees tenant-level latency budgets during maintenance windows while minimizing reserved headroom. Key capabilities: 1) per-route latency budgeting that translates to ephemeral throughput leases during drains, 2) staged node swap (micro-waves) with prewarm hooks to populate KV/prefix caches on target hosts, 3) cost-aware burst reservations with automatic release and reconciliation, 4) observability and automated rollback triggers tied to SLOs.

Proposed design:
- Latency budgets: allow customers to specify a soft latency budget (ms) per route or attach default budgets at capacity tiers. The coordinator computes a throughput lease needed to maintain budget and requests ephemeral capacity from the autoscaler for the drain period.
- Micro-wave swaps: instead of draining a whole host, the orchestrator performs micro-waves (5-15% of host slots) to traffic-shift incrementally. Each wave includes a KV/prefix cache prewarm step where the target host receives warmed prefixes for high-frequency tenants using a sampling-based prefetch.
- Prewarm protocol: integrate with KV cache service to stream top-k prefixes and recent context blobs via authenticated prewarm RPC. Prewarm has a timeboxed window and telemetry to report warm percentage.
- Cost-aware burst reservations: autoscaler exposes ephemeral burst tickets priced against a short-term reserve. The orchestrator requests only what is required by the latency budget and releases tickets immediately after warmup and wave completion. A reconciliation loop ensures tickets are released on failures.
- Safety and rollback: SLO monitors (P50/P95/P99) and error-rate detectors drive automated rollback: if any route exceeds the budget for >2 consecutive evaluation windows, the swap is paused and capacity is reverted to the old host.

Trade-offs considered:
- Extra complexity in coordinator and autoscaler vs. reduced customer impact and lower long-term reserved capacity.
- Prewarm increases network overhead and introduces potential stale state; mitigated by sampling and tight timeboxes.
- Per-tenant budgets may complicate bin-packing; initial rollout will default to tiered budgets to simplify scheduling.

Success metrics:
- Reduce maintenance-window-induced P95 latency regressions by >=60% across affected routes.
- Decrease emergency reserved headroom spend during maintenance by >=40%.
- Time-to-recover from a failed micro-wave < 2 minutes with automated rollback.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha): implement coordinator changes and basic micro-wave swap without prewarm; internal dogfood on non-production fleets.
- Phase 2 (beta): enable KV prewarm and cost-aware burst tickets; add per-route budgets and expose simple API in Console for controlled experiments.
- Phase 3 (GA): default-on for Dedicated customers with opt-out and tenant-level config knobs.

Open questions:
- Pricing model for ephemeral burst tickets and how to present cost to customers in Console.
- Limits on number of concurrent micro-waves per fleet to avoid global performance degradation.
- Exact warm percentage threshold that meaningfully reduces tail latency for large token sequences.

acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can perform micro-wave swaps at configurable wave sizes (5-20%).
Autoscaler exposes ephemeral ticket API and allows allocation/release within 30s.
KV prewarm prototype can fetch top-k prefixes and report warm_percentage.
Rollback triggers based on P95 and error-rate are functional in alpha clusters.
Dashboards surface per-wave latency and cost; alerting on rollback conditions is in place.
metrics: P95 latency delta during maintenance (target <= +10ms for budgeted routes)
Reserved headroom spend during maintenance windows (baseline vs. post-implementation)
Mean time to rollback after threshold breach (target < 2 minutes)
Warm percentage achieved within prewarm window
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal fleets, feature flag off by default, 2-week soak
Beta: select Dedicated customers opt-in with Console toggle; capture billing impact
GA: enable by default with opt-out and documentation for pricing
